summary: Community vote and moderation JSON write routes can now bind to explicitly supplied local in-memory state in the shared REST runtime adapter while default no-state routing remains an honest 501 seam.
claim_boundary: This slice proves local in-memory loopback state composition for community vote/moderation JSON write routes only. It does not claim durable Postgres/Citus persistence, transactional outbox or broker publish, Kubernetes Gateway/TLS, OpenCost allocation, ArgoCD sync/health, remote hosted CI green, branch protection, or production tenant workload deployment.

best_practice_research.used_for: Reused existing typed vote and moderation REST handlers rather than duplicating business rules in the shared runtime adapter.
Grounded the local in-memory state shape in the existing CommunityPost and VoteLedger domain types.
Preserved default no-state typed-write-plan 501 semantics while adding an explicit composed-state path.

source_basis.use: Defines vote direction, moderation verb, and receipt envelope types used by service-owned handlers.
Existing usecase enforces tenant/principal/post matching, duplicate votes, and idempotency-key vote IDs.
Route contract for community vote JSON binding.
Route contract for community moderation JSON binding.

findings: The default route catalog behavior stays simple: community vote/moderation remain typed-write-plan 501 seams unless the caller explicitly composes local state.
The state-composed path reuses existing service-owned REST typed handlers and domain vote ledger rules rather than reimplementing vote/moderation business logic in the shared runtime adapter.
The in-memory state object is explicit and caller-owned; there is no hidden global mutable state.
The slice proves the FD-001 community workload can execute vote/moderation write semantics through the shared REST runtime when a backing state seam is supplied.

The claim boundary remains compatible with Oyatie Cloud dogfood goals because local loopback state is not represented as production tenancy, cluster admission, OpenCost, or durable persistence evidence.
A regression test preserves the no-state 501 response for stateful community routes.
Positive tests require explicit seeded state for vote and moderation, and a duplicate vote proves the mutable ledger path is actually consulted.
Path/body drift checks still run before vote dispatch for /posts/{post_id}/vote.
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Removing the explicit runtime state composition would return 501 or fail the json_write route-count assertions.

findings: Callers can seed local community posts with BackboneCommunityJsonState and reuse the same router dispatch helper used by Hyper loopback tests.
Route-count fields show reviewers whether the router is default stateless or state-composed.
Focused tests cover default 501 behavior, state-composed route counts, vote success, vote duplicate rejection, and moderation success.
cargo check, unit tests, clippy -D warnings, and fmt check pass for the shared REST runtime adapter crate.

alternatives_named: Keep vote/moderation permanently 501 until Postgres is wired
Add hidden global in-memory state to the shared router
Add an explicit caller-supplied local state seam for community vote/moderation
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: The explicit local state seam proves generic JSON route binding without pretending to provide durable persistence or adding global mutable state.
rejected_reasons: Leaving the routes 501 blocks useful FD-001 loopback tenant-workload proof despite service-owned handlers already existing.
Hidden global state would make tests order-dependent and would blur the non-production claim boundary.

findings: No secrets, credentials, tokens, network endpoints, tenant records, or live infrastructure identifiers were added.
Vote and moderation requests still require explicit tenant/principal/idempotency/policy/request headers via the existing fail-closed context helpers.
The non-claim string explicitly rejects durable database, broker, cluster, OpenCost, ArgoCD sync, and live deployment claims.
Local state uses BTreeMap lookups behind a std Mutex and is intended for loopback tests only, not production throughput.
Default stateless router path has no additional state lookup for services other than community state-composed routes.
The slice touches only synthetic local test state and code; no regulated tenant data or retention policy enforcement claim is introduced.
Existing policy_decision_ref and audit/request identifiers continue to appear in JSON receipts for correlation.
Reverting removes the optional state structs, one internal path dependency, focused tests, task text, evidence, and audit rows while preserving the earlier default router behavior.
Responses keep audit_correlation_id, idempotency_key, policy_decision_ref, runtime_handler, status_code, and non_claim fields for loopback diagnostics.
The existing build_backbone_rest_router and serve_backbone_rest_microservice_listener APIs preserve default no-state semantics and existing tests.
The new build_backbone_rest_router_with_state API is additive.
New identifiers use existing BackboneRest* and community JSON/write vocabulary already present in the runtime adapter.
tasks/plan.md, tasks/todo.md, evidence, and audit-chain rows document scope and non-claims for the local state seam.
The change remains inside the shared REST runtime adapter crate plus task/evidence artifacts; service-owned domain/usecase/REST crates are reused but not modified.
The runtime adapter composes state at the adapter edge and delegates business rules to community REST/usecase/domain handlers, preserving domain boundary ownership.

The only dependency addition is an internal workspace path dependency on oya-community-post-store-domain so the adapter can hold the typed post and vote ledger required by the existing REST vote handler.
No third-party crate was added.
JSON parsing remains explicit and field-by-field; no new serde-derived API boundary or untyped domain mutation was introduced.
Moderation target_type must be post for the current local state binding.
No workflow or deployment automation was changed in this slice; local focused verification is recorded, with full local oya verify planned before submit.
